subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following statement is incorrect in respect of the Consumer Protection Act 2019? (a) This act came into force on 20th July 2020. (b) Unfair trade prohibition rules on e-commerce platforms are included in this act. (c) As per the rules of the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission no charges will be levied for complaints upto Rs. 10 lakhs.
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. Statements (a) and (b) hold: the Consumer Protection Act 2019 took effect from 20 July 2020 and covers e-commerce unfair-trade rules. Statement (c) is wrong — fee exemption for filing complaints applies up to ₹5 lakh, not ₹10 lakh, at the district commission level.

subject: General Studies
question: Which space agency has released the first visible light images of the surface of venus from space?
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. NASA's Parker Solar Probe captured the first visible-light images of Venus's surface from space during a flyby — peering through the planet's thick clouds in wavelengths our eyes can see. ESA and JAXA have Venus missions, but this particular first was NASA's.

subject: General Studies
question: 'Sustainable international financing scheme' is associated with which global association?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. The G20's sustainable finance agenda includes schemes to channel international financing toward climate and development goals — the phrase in the stem maps to that grouping, not ASEAN, BRICS, or SAARC.

subject: General Studies
question: NROL-85, which was launched recently, is an intelligence satellite of which country?
explanation: NROL-85 हा अमेरिकेच्या नॅशनल रिकॉनिसन्स ऑफिसचा (NRO) गुप्तहेर उपग्रह आहे. हा उपग्रह एप्रिल २०२२ मध्ये कॅलिफोर्नियातील व्हँडेनबर्ग स्पेस फोर्स बेसवरून स्पेसएक्स (SpaceX) च्या फाल्कन ९ रॉकेटद्वारे प्रक्षेपित करण्यात आला होता.

subject: General Studies
question: India's First RT-PCR kit to detect the Omicron Variant, named 'Omisure' is developed by which company?
explanation: On this one, option A. Tata MD developed 'Omisure', India's first RT-PCR kit to detect the Omicron variant of COVID-19. Piramal, Sun Pharma, and Apex Pharma were distractors from the wider pharma space.

subject: General Studies
question: Identify the person from the following description: (a) In 2013 she acted in the film 'Mai' for the first time. (b) The first Indian singer to be nominated for a Grammy Award. (c) She was recently awarded the Maharashtra Bhushan Award 2021.
explanation: Go with option B. Asha Bhosale acted in the 2013 film 'Mai', was the first Indian singer nominated for a Grammy, and received the Maharashtra Bhushan Award 2021 — all three clues point to her, not Lata Mangeshkar or the other names.

subject: Economy
question: Which institution has developed the 'Positive Pay System (PPS)' for Cheque Payment?
explanation: Pick option A. NPCI developed the Positive Pay System for cheque truncation — account holders pre-confirm high-value cheque details before payment clears. RBI mandated it, but the technical system came from NPCI, not Niti Aayog or the Finance Ministry.

subject: General Studies
question: Which one of the following country has provided instrumental support to India's ambitious space mission 'Gaganyan'?
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. France has been a key partner for Gaganyaan — supplying equipment, training Indian astronauts, and supporting human-spaceflight infrastructure. Japan, South Korea, and UAE cooperate on other space fronts but France led this crewed-mission support.

subject: General Studies
question: Who has been appointed as the chairman of the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA)?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Ajay Bhushan Pandey — former Finance Secretary — was appointed chairman of the National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), the audit-oversight body for listed companies and large firms. Nilekani, Premji, and Gopalakrishnan were never NFRA chairs.

subject: General Studies
question: The Supreme Court has appointed Justice R.V. Ravindran Committee in October 2021 for which of the following purpose?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. In October 2021 the Supreme Court set up the Justice R.V. Ravindran committee to probe the Pegasus spyware snooping allegations. It was not for IPL fixing, Aadhaar policy, or any of the other listed purposes.

subject: General Studies
question: Which Union Ministry launched 'My CGHS' Mobile application?
explanation: The right pick is option B. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched the 'My CGHS' mobile app for Central Government Health Scheme beneficiaries — booking appointments, viewing records, and accessing empanelled hospitals. Education, Tourism, and Culture ministries have no CGHS mandate.

subject: General Studies
question: Which country launched the 'COMPETES ACT' of 2022?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. The America COMPETES Act of 2022 is US legislation aimed at boosting semiconductor manufacturing, R&D, and competitiveness against China — a congressional package, not a Russian, UK, or Australian law.

subject: General Studies
question: 16th World Youth Archery Championship was held in August 2021 in which of the following nation?
explanation: On this one, option B. The 16th World Youth Archery Championship was held in Wrocław, Poland, in August 2021. South Korea, India, and Australia have hosted other archery events but not this edition.

subject: General Studies
question: Who has been awarded the 'International Gandhi Award for Leprosy-2021'?
explanation: Go with option A. Dr Bhushan Kumar received the International Gandhi Award for Leprosy 2021 for his work in leprosy control. Dr G.P. Talwar, Dr M.D. Gupte, and Dr Atul Shah are respected names in the field but the 2021 award went to Dr Bhushan Kumar.

subject: Geography
question: According to livestock census 2019, what is the rank of Maharashtra in terms of livestock among the country?
explanation: Pick option C. The 20th Livestock Census (2019) ranked Maharashtra seventh among states by total livestock population — behind leaders like Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. First, third, and ninth are common traps from other census rankings.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following are the correct statements regarding the tenure of a Governor of the State? (a) Governor remains in his office as long as President of India wishes. (b) Governor may resign voluntarily. (c) The appointment of Governor is generally for 05 years. (d) Governor remains in his office until another person takes charge.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Every statement on gubernatorial tenure is constitutionally sound: a Governor holds office during the President's pleasure, may resign, is normally appointed for five years, and continues until a successor enters — Articles 156 and 157 together cover all four points.

subject: Polity
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution defines the duties of the Chief Minister?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Article 167 spells out the Chief Minister's duties toward the Governor — furnishing information, recommending legislative business, and communicating Council of Ministers' decisions. Article 163 covers CM–Governor relations broadly; 164 deals with appointment, not duties.

subject: Polity
question: New responsibilities given to Gram Panchayats as per 73rd Constitution Amendment Act, 1993. (a) Enforcement of Land Reforms Act (b) To develop forest industries, small and cottage industries (c) Facilitate technical and vocational education (d) To arrange entertainment for the people of the village Which of the above statement/statements is/are incorrect?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 Panchayat subjects — land reforms, cottage industries, and vocational education appear there. Arranging village entertainment is not a constitutional Panchayat function, so only statement (d) is incorrect.

subject: Polity
question: Elections in India for Parliament and State Legislatures are conducted by _______.
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Article 324 vests the conduct of elections to Parliament and state legislatures in the Election Commission of India. The President appoints governors; State Election Commissions handle panchayat and municipal polls — not Lok Sabha or Vidhan Sabha seats.

subject: Polity
question: Which of the following Committee is not related to the Panchayati Raj?
explanation: The right pick is option B. Rajmannar Committee (1971) examined Centre–State relations in Tamil Nadu's context — not Panchayati Raj reform. Ashok Mehta, Thungan, and L.M. Singhvi committees all fed directly into strengthening local self-government.

subject: Polity
question: Which article states that each state shall have an Advocate General?
explanation: On this one, option D. Article 165 provides that each state shall have an Advocate General — the chief legal adviser to the state government. Articles 177, 194, and 197 cover other state-legislature and service matters, not this office.

subject: Polity
question: Who among the following was the members of the drafting committee of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Go with option C. Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer was a member of the Constituent Assembly's Drafting Committee under B.R. Ambedkar. Patel, Nehru, and Rajendra Prasad chaired or presided but were not on that seven-member drafting panel.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following statements are true regarding the development of transport infrastructure in India? (a) The Public Work Department was created during the time of Lord Dalhousie. (b) During the reigns of Lord Cornwallis and John Shore road construction gained momentum. (c) Broad gauge tracks were built during the early days of the railway. (d) Nagpur Council presented 'Twenty Years Road Development Programme' to the Government.
explanation: The right pick is option B. Lord Dalhousie set up the Public Works Department and the Nagpur Road Plan framed a twenty-year road programme — statements (a) and (d) hold. Cornwallis and John Shore are not credited with a major road push in standard texts, and broad-gauge as an 'early railway' claim is what drops (b) and (c) from the set.

subject: History
question: Match the pair. (a) 1890, Mumbai Mill Workers Union - (i) Lala Lajpatrai (b) 1918, Ahmadabad Textile Labour Association - (ii) B.P. Wadiya (c) 1918, Madras Labour Union - (iii) Mahatma Gandhi (d) 1920, All India Trade Union Congress - (iv) Narayan Meghaji Lokhande
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Narayan Meghaji Lokhande led the 1890 Mumbai Mill Workers Union, Gandhi shaped the 1918 Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association, B.P. Wadiya organised the Madras Labour Union the same year, and Lala Lajpat Rai was linked with the 1920 AITUC — code (iv), (iii), (ii), (i).

subject: Polity
question: Which among the following features of Indian Constitution is not borrowed from British Constitution?
explanation: Pick option D. Parliamentary government, Cabinet system, and Rule of Law all came from British constitutional practice. The Concurrent List — shared legislative field for Centre and States — was taken from the Government of India Act 1935 / Australian federal model, not Westminster.

subject: Polity
question: Match the pair place of the Congress Session and his Presidents name. (a) First Congress Session, Mumbai (1885) - (i) George Yul (b) Second Congress Session, Calcutta (1886) - (ii) Badruddin Tayyabji (c) Third Congress Session, Madras (1887) - (iii) Womeshchandra Banarjee (d) Fourth Congress Session, Allahabad (1888) - (iv) Dadabhai Naoroji
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Bombay 1885 went to Womesh Chandra Banerjee, Calcutta 1886 to Dadabhai Naoroji, Madras 1887 to Badruddin Tyabji, and Allahabad 1888 to George Yule — the first English president — giving (iii), (iv), (ii), (i).

subject: General Studies
question: Government of India Act of 1935 provided for establishment of which institutes? (a) Federal Court (b) Reserve Bank of India (c) Federal Railway (d) High Commissioner
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for a Federal Court, the Reserve Bank of India, and a Federal Railway authority — the High Commissioner post belonged to the earlier 1919 framework, not this Act.

subject: General Studies
question: In 1847 who was the first to demand the launch of a railway connecting the Mumbai port and the cotton producing regions?
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. In 1847 the British free-trade advocate John Bright pressed for a railway linking the Bombay port with cotton-growing hinterland — an early commercial case for Indian rail expansion.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following was the aim of 'Trading Economy' of British Government? (a) No Trading competition (b) Maximum profit (c) Control on economic factors (d) Economic growth of India Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
explanation: On this one, option D. The British 'trading economy' in India was built around extracting maximum profit for the Company and Crown — monopoly, control, and Indian industrial growth were means or side-effects, not the stated aim in colonial policy.

subject: General Studies
question: What Dr. Bhau Daji Lad was the proponent of?
explanation: Go with option C. Dr Bhau Daji Lad — physician, scholar, and associate of the Paramhans Sabha — was a vocal champion of widow remarriage and social reform in mid-nineteenth-century Bombay.

subject: General Studies
question: Choose the correct option by matching the following: (a) Acharya Bal Shastri Jambhekar - (i) Establishment of Manav Dharm Sabha at Surat (b) Durgaram Manchharam, Dadoba Pandurang - (ii) Purification of Shripad Sheshadri Paralikar who was in the custody of Christi Missionary (c) Annie Besant - (iii) Establishment of Normal School and Victoria Institute (d) Keshavchandra Sen - (iv) Establishment of Central Hindu-College
explanation: Pick option B. According to the answer key the pairs run (ii), (i), (iv), (iii) — Jambhekar with (ii), Dadoba–Durgaram with Manav Dharm Sabha at Surat, Annie Besant with Central Hindu College, and Keshav Chandra Sen with (iii). Match from the list the paper gave rather than reshuffling from memory.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following organizers of the Secret Militant Organizations in Maharashtra and their areas. (a) Shridhar Paranjape - (i) Amravati (b) Dr. Siddhanath Kane - (ii) Belgaum (c) Dadasaheb Khaparde - (iii) Wardha and Nagpur (d) Gangadhar Deshpande - (iv) Yavatmal
explanation: The right pick is option C. Shridhar Paranjape worked around Wardha–Nagpur, Gangadhar Deshpande in the Belgaum belt, Dadasaheb Khaparde in Amravati, and Dr Siddhanath Kane in Yavatmal — secret militant networks mapped as (iii), (iv), (i), (ii).

subject: History
question: Which of the following statements are false regarding revolt of Santhala? (a) Economic exploitation of Santhala is presented in Punjab Review. (b) Santhala declared the decision of establishment of 'State of Truth'. (c) Kanhu the leader of Santhala was treacherously kidnapped. (d) O Mauli, the officer gave the report of duel of Santhala.
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. The Santhal revolt did declare a 'State of Truth' and O Mauli's report on the struggle is on record — statements (a) about the Punjab Review and (c) about Kanhu's treacherous kidnapping are the false pair.

subject: General Studies
question: Who made the following statements which caused the growth of Communalism? (a) Hindu and Muslim are two nations and these are two opposite countries. (b) The policy of divide and beat has to be adopted in India and Muslims should be kept away from Hindu. (c) Mahatma Gandhiji's Civil-Disobedience Movement is not totally for freedom of India but to keep Indian Muslims under the domination of Hindu Mahasabha. (d) Those who are recognizing India as their motherland, India is their nation.

options.A: Principal Bake, Sir Sayyad Ahamad, V.D. Sawarkar, Mohamad Ali Jinnah
options.B: Sir Sayyad Ahamad, Principal Bake, Mohamad Ali Jinnah, V.D. Sawarkar
options.C: V.D. Sawarkar, Mohamad Ali Jinnah, Principal Bake, Sir Sayyad Ahamad
options.D: Mohamad Ali Jinnah, Sir Sayyad Ahmad, V.D. Sawarkar, Principal Bake

explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Statement (a) — two nations — fits Sir Syed Ahmad; (b) divide-and-beat goes to Principal Beck; (c) the attack on Civil Disobedience to Mohammad Ali Jinnah; and (d) motherland nationhood to V.D. Savarkar.

subject: History
question: Identify the person from following description: (a) He started the Newspaper 'India' (b) Establishment of Bombay Association (c) Establishment of East India Association (d) President of Indian National Congress
explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Dadabhai Naoroji started the paper 'India', helped form the Bombay Association, founded the East India Association in London, and presided over the Indian National Congress — all four clues point to the 'Grand Old Man'.

subject: General Studies
question: Gopal Ganesh Agarkar was related with which of the following Newspapers? (a) Kesari and Maratha (b) Varhad Samachar (c) Sudharak (d) Swarajya Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Gopal Ganesh Agarkar edited or founded Kesari and Maratha (with Tilak), brought out Varhad Samachar, and ran Sudharak — Swarajya is not counted among his papers in the standard list.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following personalities were related with Bombay Presidency Association Organisation? (a) Gopal Ganesh Agarkar (b) Firojshah Mehta (c) Badruddin Tayyabji (d) Justice Telang
explanation: Go with option B. The Bombay Presidency Association drew in Firozshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji, and Justice Telang — Agarkar was active in other reform circles but not listed among its core founders in textbook accounts.

subject: General Studies
question: What was the aim of East India Association organisation, established on 1 November 1866? (a) Female Education (b) Political Education (c) People Education (d) Religious Education Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
explanation: On this one, option C. Dadabhai Naoroji's East India Association (1 November 1866) aimed at political awakening and educating British and Indian public opinion on Indian affairs — 'people education' in the broad civic sense, not a female- or religion-only brief.

subject: General Studies
question: In India _______ is called as a 'Golden Fiber' crop.
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Jute is called the 'golden fibre' for its silky lustre and value in sacking and packaging — cotton is 'white gold', wool and silk carry different labels.

subject: General Studies
question: In the decade of 1911 to 1921 the Population Growth in the State of Maharashtra was negative. The reason behind it is _______.

options.A: Low birth rate during that period

explanation: Pick option B. Maharashtra's population growth turned negative in the 1911–1921 decade chiefly because the influenza pandemic after World War I pushed up mortality — not low birth rate, floods, or lack of industry alone.

subject: Geography
question: Which is the mountain/hill situated on the North-South direction of western Maharashtra?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. The Sahyadri (Western Ghats) run north–south along western Maharashtra, forming the state's coastal–plateau divide; Satpura lies further east, Satmala and Shambhu Mahadev are sub-ranges, not the main N–S chain.

subject: General Studies
question: Following statements are correct or incorrect? (a) Commercialisation of agriculture did not promote capitalist - agriculture. (b) Commercialisation of agriculture intensified tenancy and share-cropping.

options.C: (a) is false and (b) is true statement
options.D: (a) is true and (b) is false statement

explanation: The verified answer here is option B. According to the answer key, both statements are false: commercialisation of agriculture did promote capitalist farming and the tenancy–share-cropping link in (b) is also rejected in the paper's framing. If your textbook wording differs, defer to the key for this item.

subject: Geography
question: Iron ore reserves in Maharashtra are located in the district of _______.
explanation: The right pick is option D. Maharashtra's workable iron-ore reserves are concentrated in the Sindhudurg–Gadchiroli belt on the Konkan–Vidarbha fringe; Wardha, Nashik, and Buldhana are not the districts named for ore in state geography notes.

subject: General Studies
question: One of the following is an important port situated on the west coast of India.
explanation: Pick option C. Kandla (Deendayal Port) sits on the Gulf of Kutch on India's west coast; Chennai, Haldia, and Kolkata are east-coast or Hooghly ports.

subject: General Studies
question: What is the percent share of tourism in India's domestic income as of 2019?
explanation: Go with option D. Tourism's share in India's domestic income around 2019 was about 9.34% per the figures MPSC expected — the 7–9% band in other options are close but not the precise statistic on the key.

subject: General Studies
question: Following are some of the problems in the agriculture sector in Maharashtra. Which one is more social in nature?
explanation: On this one, option D. Fragmentation of farmland is rooted in inheritance customs and family division — a social–institutional problem — whereas weather, research gaps, and capital shortage are economic or technical constraints.

subject: Reasoning
question: The average highest temperature in the month of May is recorded in _______ region of Maharashtra.
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Eastern Vidarbha lies in the rain-shadowed interior Deccan and records the state's highest average May temperatures, while the coast and western Maharashtra stay relatively moderated by proximity to the sea.

subject: General Studies
question: Bhilai Iron and Steel Industry is located in the state of _______.
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. The Bhilai Steel Plant, built with Soviet collaboration under the Second Plan, stands near Bhilai in present-day Chhattisgarh (carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000). West Bengal has Durgapur; Odisha has Rourkela — Bhilai belongs to the Chhattisgarh belt.

subject: Geography
question: Which of the following physiographic factor predominantly influence on climate of Maharashtra?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. The Sahyadri (Western Ghats) wall and the Satpuda range steer the southwest monsoon, orographic rain, and temperature contrasts across Konkan, plateau, and Vidarbha. The Deccan plateau and coastal plains matter locally, but these two ranges dominate Maharashtra's climate pattern.

subject: General Studies
question: The population is decreasing continuously in rural area, because: (a) The birth rate in rural area is low. (b) The rural people are migrating to urban area. (c) The employment is not available in rural area. (d) The death rate is high in rural area. Which statement/s of the above is true?
explanation: The right pick is option B. Rural headcount falls mainly because people move out to towns and cities for work and services — out-migration, not a uniquely low rural birth rate or a high rural death rate by itself. Employment scarcity (c) often pushes migration, but the keyed statement is the direct demographic fact: only (b).

subject: General Studies
question: When State Government in Maharashtra has declared the Blue Revolution Mission?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Maharashtra declared its Blue Revolution (Neeli Kranti) Mission in 2017 to expand inland and marine fisheries, cold chains, and fish exports. The 2018–2020 years are near-miss distractors around the actual launch.

subject: Geography
question: The multipurpose project of Gujarat 'Ukai' is situated on which River?
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Ukai Dam — a major multipurpose project in south Gujarat — is built across the Tapti (Tapi) river near Ukai village. Sabarmati, Mahi, and Narmada host other famous dams but not Ukai.

subject: General Studies
question: In which state the number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies was highest at the end of March 2020?
explanation: On this one, option D. NABARD data for March 2020 placed Maharashtra at the top among States in the number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) — the short-term rural credit network is densest here. Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat rank lower on that count.

subject: General Studies
question: The Government appointed a Committee in 1993 on Disinvestment in Public Sector Enterprises under the Chairmanship of _______.
explanation: Go with option C. The Rangarajan Committee (1993) framed the early policy roadmap for disinvestment in public-sector enterprises under the Narasimha Rao reforms. G.V. Ramakrishna chaired a later Disinvestment Commission; Montek Ahluwalia and C.P. Chandrashekhar led other panels.

subject: General Studies
question: During 2017-18 Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was highest 23.6 percent in _______ sector in India.
explanation: Pick option A. In 2017–18 communication services — telecom, media, and related digital infrastructure — drew the largest FDI share at about 23.6%, ahead of manufacturing and financial services. That spike reflected spectrum auctions, data growth, and liberalised telecom FDI norms.

subject: Economy
question: To tackle the burgeoning problem of air pollution, the 2021-22 Budget proposes to provide an amount of Rs. 2217 crore for _______ urban centres with a million-plus population.
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Union Budget 2021–22 earmarked Rs 2,217 crore for air-quality management across 42 million-plus urban centres — cities above ten lakh population where pollution monitoring and mitigation were prioritised. The 32, 52, and 62 counts are arithmetic distractors.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following: (a) Second largest agro based industry in India - (i) Cotton industry (b) One of the oldest and organised industry in India - (ii) Iron and steel industry (c) Industry leading to rapid industrialisation - (iii) Sugar industry (d) Use of new technology - (iv) Automobile industry
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Match by industry profile: sugar is India's second-largest agro-based industry (a–iii); cotton textiles are among the oldest organised mills (b–i); iron and steel drove heavy industrialisation (c–ii); the automobile sector absorbed modern technology fastest (d–iv).

subject: General Studies
question: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has a right to order conduct of supplementary audit and he may also comment upon the audit report within _______ days from the date of receipt of audit report.
explanation: The right pick is option B. Under CAG audit rules the Comptroller and Auditor General may order supplementary audit and must submit comments on the audit report within 60 days of receiving it — not 30, 90, or 120. MPSC often tests this fixed timeline.

subject: General Studies
question: Consider the following statements in the context of Seventh Finance Commission for distribution of the states share of the central excise duty: (a) 25 percent weightage for population. (b) 33.5 percent weightage for poor in each state. (c) 16.5 percent weightage for increase in the per capita income of the state. (d) 25 percent weightage for income equalisation between state. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. For sharing central excise duty the Seventh Finance Commission gave 25% weight to population (a) and 25% to income equalisation between States (d). The 33.5% 'poor' weight and 16.5% per-capita-income-growth weight belong to a different formula — not this excise-sharing scheme.

subject: History
question: Consider the following statements: (a) Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana (SGRY) was launched September 2001. (b) Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) was introduced in February 2006. (c) The Nehru Rozgar Yojana (NRY) was launched in October 1989 for the benefit of the rural poor. Which of the following statement/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: Go with option C. SGRY was launched in September 2001 by merging earlier rural wage schemes, and MGNREGS/NREGA rolled out from February 2006 — both dates in the stem are correct. NRY (1989) is also true historically, but the keyed pair is (a) and (b) only.

subject: Polity
question: Consider the following statements: (a) The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (Amendment) Act, passed by the Parliament in 2021. (b) The deposit insurance premium is recovered from the depositors. (c) The deposit insurance premium is compulsory for all insured banks. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?

options.D: All of the above are correct

explanation: On this one, option B. Parliament passed the DICGC (Amendment) Act in 2021 (a), and the deposit-insurance premium is compulsory for all insured banks (c) — but the premium is paid by banks to DICGC, not recovered from depositors, so (b) is wrong.

subject: Economy
question: The difference between fiscal deficit and interest payment during the year is called _______.
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments on past borrowing — it shows how much of today's borrowing funds current spending excluding debt-service. Fiscal and revenue deficits measure different gaps; budget deficit is a broader informal term.

subject: Economy
question: N.K. Singh Committee of 2016 is related to _______.

options.D: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act

explanation: Pick option D. The N.K. Singh Committee (2016) reviewed the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act and recommended a debt-to-GDP anchor and escape clauses — not a Finance Commission or Five-Year Plan. FRBM compliance is a recurring MPSC budget topic.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following were the reasons for small land holdings during 1980 to 1985 in India? (a) Law of inheritance (b) Rapidly growing population (c) Rural indebtedness (d) Rapidly growing joint family system
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Fragmentation grew through inheritance laws splitting holdings (a), population pressure on the same land (b), and distress sales or debt forcing subdivision (c). A growing joint-family system (d) would tend to keep land together — the opposite of smaller plots.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following is not objective of National Population Policy 2000?

options.D: Incentive to adopt two child small family

explanation: The right pick is option C. National Population Policy 2000 targets lower infant mortality, universal immunisation, and incentives for a two-child norm — mid-day meals for poor children belong to the education/nutrition scheme, not NPP objectives.

subject: Economy
question: During which five year plan three major steel plants in the public sector were built up at Rourkela, Bhilai and Durgapur?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Rourkela, Bhilai, and Durgapur — the three integrated public-sector steel plants with foreign collaboration — were core projects of the Second Five Year Plan (1956–61). The First Plan focused on irrigation and agriculture; the Third carried forward other heavy industry.

subject: Reasoning
question: Which of the following is not a quantitative monetary measure of Reserve Bank of India?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Bank rate, CRR, and SLR are quantitative tools — they change the volume or cost of bank reserves and credit by fixed rules. Moral suasion is qualitative: the RBI persuades banks without a mandatory ratio or rate change.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following substance has the highest thermal conductivity?
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Among common solids, silver has the highest thermal conductivity — free electrons carry heat efficiently. Aluminium conducts well but ranks below silver; wood and glass are thermal insulators by comparison.

question: Light enters the eye through thin membrane called the _______.
explanation: डोळ्यामध्ये प्रकाश हा बाहेरील पारदर्शक पटलातून म्हणजेच कॉर्निया (पारपटल / Cornea) मधून प्रवेश करतो. कॉर्निया हा डोळ्याच्या सर्वात बाहेरील संरक्षणात्मक थर असून तो प्रकाशाचे जास्तीत जास्त अपवर्तन (Refraction) करतो.

subject: General Studies
question: Echo is heard if the distance between the source of sound and the obstacle is _______.

options.B: More than or equal to 17 meters

explanation: Go with option B. At roughly 340 m/s in air, sound needs about 0.05 s to travel 17 m and return — the minimum path for a distinct echo. Distances below 17 m merge the reflected sound with the direct note; 17 m or more separates them clearly.

subject: Science
question: In _______ model of an atom, the angular momentum (mvr) of an electron is an integral multiple of the quantity h/2π.
explanation: Pick option C. Bohr's model quantises angular momentum as mvr = n(h/2π) — only certain orbits are allowed. Rutherford had the nuclear atom without quantisation; Dalton treated atoms as indivisible spheres; Fermi is linked to nuclear statistics, not this orbital rule.

subject: Science
question: Choose the incorrect answer:

options.B: The electron density in the internuclear region in bonding molecular orbital is very low.
options.C: Energy of the antibonding molecular orbital is higher than that of the combining atomic orbitals.
options.D: Antibonding molecular orbitals are represented by σ*, π*, δ*, etc.

explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. In a bonding molecular orbital electron density rises in the internuclear region — that is why the bond forms. Statement (B) wrongly says density there is very low; that description fits an antibonding orbital. Options A, C, and D state standard MO theory correctly.

subject: Science
question: During biological nitrogen fixation, nitrifying bacteria convert _______.
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Nitrifying bacteria oxidise ammonium (NH₄⁺) stepwise to nitrate (NO₃⁻) — that is nitrification, not the conversion of atmospheric N₂ to ammonia. The stem mixes the term 'nitrogen fixation' with nitrifiers; follow the key's NH₄⁺ → NO₃⁻ pairing.

subject: General Studies
question: Match the following: (a) Python molurus - (i) Haemotoxic (b) Naja naja - (ii) Blind snake (c) Viper russelli - (iii) Neurotoxic (d) Typhlops braminus - (iv) Non-poisonous
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. Python molurus (Indian rock python) is non-poisonous; Naja naja (cobra) is neurotoxic; Viper russelli (Russell's viper) is haemotoxic; Typhlops braminus is the blind snake — giving (iv), (iii), (i), (ii).

subject: General Studies
question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of larval stages of Aurelia?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Aurelia (jellyfish) life cycle runs Planula → Hydratuba → Scyphistoma → Ephyra — the polyp scyphistoma stage precedes the free-swimming ephyra medusa.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following is/are group/groups of reptilian animals? (a) Lizard, Snake, Frog and Loris (b) Turtle, Gharial, Caiman and Tuatara (c) Turtle, Crocodile, Salamander and Lizard (d) Salamander, Catotes, Turtle and Frog
explanation: The right pick is option A. Only group (b) — Turtle, Gharial, Caiman and Tuatara — are all reptiles. The other lists mix in amphibians (Frog, Salamander) or a mammal (Loris).

subject: Geography
question: Irrigation in the fields of saline tract affects the productivity of crops because of: (a) Degradation of soil structure (b) Growth inhibition of plants (c) Leaf discolouration (d) Salt accumulation in soil Which of the given above statement/statements is/are correct?
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Saline-tract irrigation degrades soil structure and lets salts accumulate in the root zone — both (a) and (d). Leaf discolouration alone is not the pair the answer key selects.

subject: General Studies
question: How the occurrence of Endemic pest is defined?

options.C: Occurs in the same area year after year
options.D: Occurs in an area in severe form

explanation: The verified answer here is option C. An endemic pest appears in the same locality year after year at a steady level — not merely 'severe' or 'in a few places' for one season.

subject: General Studies
question: Plants whose seeds are naked, are classified in which group?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. Gymnosperms bear naked seeds — not enclosed in a fruit — unlike angiosperms. Tracheophyta is the broader vascular-plant division.

subject: Science
question: From the following viruses, which one transfers from one person to other via infected needles or unprotected sex?
explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Hepatitis B spreads through infected blood, needles and unprotected sex. Dengue and Hepatitis A use different routes; Rota virus mainly causes childhood diarrhoea.

subject: General Studies
question: Which scientist discovered small pox vaccine?
explanation: एडवर्ड जेनर (Edward Jenner) यांनी १७९६ मध्ये गोवर/गोमाता (Cowpox) विषाणूचा वापर करून देवीच्या (Smallpox) लसीचा शोध लावला. म्हणूनच त्यांना "इम्युनॉलॉजीचे जनक" (Father of Immunology) मानले जाते.

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following is used to disinfect surfaces?
explanation: The examiner has marked option A. Ultraviolet (UV) light is widely used to disinfect exposed surfaces. Autoclaving is for heat sterilisation of instruments, not routine surface wipe-down.

subject: General Studies
question: Mango tree is in the middle of Gauva and Lemon tree. Papaya tree is near the Lemon tree but not near the Mango tree and Gauva tree. At the right side of Papaya tree is Coconut tree but at the left side of Gauva tree no any tree. Which statement/s of following is/are correct? (i) Lemon tree is between the Papaya and Mango tree. explanation: Working through it, option D is the one. Left to right the row is Guava–Mango–Lemon–Papaya–Coconut: Lemon sits between Mango and Papaya, Papaya between Lemon and Coconut, and Papaya is next to Coconut — all three statements hold.

subject: General Studies
question: Find out which assumption is correct from the given statement. (ii) Many people take seriously the warning given on cigarette packet.

options.D: Both (i) and (ii) assumptions are not correct

explanation: The verified answer here is option C. The warning on a cigarette pack only works if people read it and take it seriously — both assumptions (i) and (ii) must hold for the label to serve its purpose.

subject: Reasoning
question: The percentage distribution of passengers in different trains are shown in a pie-chart: Train A: 13%, Train Q: 19%, Train R: 9%, Train S: 24%, Train M: 20%, Train L: 15%. Total number of passengers = 8500. What is the average number of passengers in Trains S, M and L together?
explanation: Straight to the answer — option C. Trains S, M and L carry 24% + 20% + 15% = 59% of 8500, i.e. 5015 passengers; divided by 3 gives 1672 on average.

subject: Reasoning
question: There are 80 players in a club, of which 36 play Kabaddi and 48 play Cricket. If 12 players play both Kabaddi and Cricket, what is the percentage of players who do not play either Kabaddi or Cricket?
explanation: The right pick is option C. Kabaddi or Cricket (or both) cover 36 + 48 − 12 = 72 players; 80 − 72 = 8 play neither — 8/80 × 100 = 10%.

question: Find the average of natural numbers between 1 to 97.
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. Natural numbers 1 through 97 average to (1 + 97) ÷ 2 = 49 — the midpoint of an arithmetic sequence.

subject: General Studies
question: If A and B together can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B alone in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
explanation: The right pick is option A. 1/15 = 1/A + 1/20, so 1/A = 1/60 and A alone finishes in 60 days.

subject: General Studies
question: A train 250 metres long running at a speed 45 km/hr, how long does it take to pass a platform of length 250 metres?
explanation:
एकूण पार करावयाचे अंतर = आगगाडीची लांबी + प्लॅटफॉर्मची लांबी = २५० + २५० = ५०० मीटर.
वेग = ४५ किमी/तास = ४५ × (५/१८) = १२.५ मीटर/सेकंद.
लागणारा वेळ = अंतर ÷ वेग = ५०० ÷ १२.५ = ४० सेकंद.

question: A man goes to Mumbai from Pune at a speed of 4 km/hr and returns to Pune at a speed of 6 km/hr. What is his average speed of the entire journey?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Equal distances at 4 km/h and 6 km/h give average speed 2 × 4 × 6 ÷ (4 + 6) = 4.8 km/h — not the simple mean of the two speeds.

subject: Science
question: The modern periodic table is based on _______.

explanation: Moseley and the modern periodic law order elements by atomic number (proton count)—resolving anomalies of Newlands' octaves and Mendeleev's atomic-mass table. Atomic mass alone, triads, and octave rules are pre-modern schemes superseded by Z-based arrangement.

subject: History
question: Dr. Ambedkar demanded for _______ in Round Table Conference.
explanation: The correct answer is option A — at the Round Table Conferences Dr Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for Depressed Classes—leading to the Communal Award and Poona Pact negotiations. subject: History
question: In 1899 A.D. _______ started 'Anatha Balikashram'.
explanation: Dhondo Keshav Karve started Anath Balikashram in 1899 at Pune—for orphaned and destitute girls, precursor to wider women's education institutions. Phule's 1848 school, Shahu's grants, and Gaikwad's Baroda reforms belong to different dates and patrons.

subject: Current Affairs
question: Who was given 'Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award 2007'?
explanation: Option B is correct because M. S. Dhoni received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna for 2007—the highest sporting honour that year after India's T20 World Cup triumph. subject: Current Affairs
question: Hamas is a militant organisation fighting against which of the following countries?
explanation: Hamas is the Palestinian militant and political organisation whose armed wing fights Israel—especially in Gaza conflicts. Sudan, Brazil, and Syria are not the primary adversarial state pairing in Hamas's core conflict narrative.

subject: Science
question: What is the range of Agni – III ballistic missile?
explanation: The answer is option A: agni-III is an intermediate-range ballistic missile with a range of about 3,500 km—covering regional targets from mobile launchers. subject: Polity
question: What is contained in a parliamentary form of government?
explanation: Choose option B: Parliamentary government means the executive is responsible to the legislature—Council of Ministers holds office while enjoying majority support in the Lok Sabha/Assembly. 'Executive controls legislature' describes presidential or authoritarian systems; judiciary-control options invert separation of powers. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

subject: Economy
question: NABARD is a _______.
explanation: Option B is the right choice since NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) is a development bank—refinancing cooperatives and rural credit, not a mere board, bureau, or department. Established 1982 on Shivaraman Committee recommendations; 'bank' is the institutional form correct. subject: Science
question: In photosynthesis, water and carbon dioxide combine to form _______.
explanation: You want Carbohydrates on this one. Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose; the overall equation is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, driven by chlorophyll in chloroplasts. For MPSC prelims, one line of revision is enough to lock this fact into memory — add it to your one-page factual notebook.

subject: History
question: Who was the commander of a battalion 'Rani of Jhansi' in Azad Hind Sena?
explanation: Option A works here because Dr Lakshmi Swaminathan (Sehgal) commanded the Rani of Jhansi Regiment in Subhas Bose's Indian National Army—women's combat unit of the Azad Hind Fauj. Sarojini Naidu, Shanti Ghosh, and Pritilata Waddedar served nationalism through other roles without this INA battalion command. explanation: Straight to the answer: 14.02. This kind of item rewards steady factual reading over aggressive shortcut techniques — the marks come from having read the source once, not from clever elimination.

subject: Geography
question: _______ is a thermal power station in Maharashtra.
explanation: Option B matches the question because the Dabhol power project (Ratnagiri district) was a major gas/thermal power station on Maharashtra's Konkan coast—Enron-era landmark. question: In _______ Dhondo Keshav Karve started 'Vidhava Vivahottejak Mandal'.
explanation: The answer is option C: Karve founded the Widow Remarriage Encouragement Association (Vidhava Vivah Uttejak Mandal) in 1893 at Pune—predating the Women's University and Anath Balikashram expansion. 1873 and 1887 are early reform years; 1899 marks Anath Balikashram, not this Mandal. subject: Science
question: Sound waves do not travel through _______.
explanation: Sound needs a material medium—solids, liquids, or gases—to propagate as mechanical waves. A vacuum lacks particles to transmit compressions; therefore sound cannot travel through vacuum—option D is the non-medium choice among the four states listed.

subject: Science
question: Which is the structural formula of Acetylene?
explanation: Choose option B: acetylene (ethyne) has the formula H−C≡C−H—a triple bond between two carbons with terminal hydrogens. H−C=C−H is ethylene (double bond); CH₄ and ethane-like structures lack the C≡C core that defines alkynes. Distractors A (H−C=C−H), C (H₂C=CH₂ (Ethylene structure)), D (CH₄ (Methane-like structure)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. subject: History
question: The 'Queen's Proclamation' was declared in _______.
explanation: Queen Victoria's Proclamation transferring India from the Company to the Crown was read at Allahabad on 1 November 1858—ending Company rule after 1857. December 1885 is first Congress; 1905 Bengal partition; August 1947 Independence.

subject: History
question: Who among the following Peshwa's was popularly known as a Nanasaheb?
explanation: Option C works here because Balaji Baji Rao (Nana Saheb Peshwa I) ruled 1740–1761—third Peshwa, son of Baji Rao I, defeated at Panipat 1761. Baji Rao I was the second Peshwa; Balaji Vishwanath the first; Raghunath Rao the later usurper—not the popular 'Nanasaheb' tag. Distractors A (Baji Rao), B (Balaji Vishwanath), D (Raghunath Rao) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. subject: Geography
question: Which of the following rivers in Maharashtra is flowing westward?
explanation: The official Set A key selects Tapi. The Tapi river is one of only three major peninsular rivers that flow west; it rises at Multai in MP and drains into the Arabian Sea through Gujarat. The three wrong options are the standard distractor set MPSC uses for this topic — one is a chronological neighbour, one is a thematic near-miss and one is a plausible-sounding invention.

subject: General Studies
question: Out of total area of India, it is necessary to have _______ per cent area under forest.
explanation: The answer is option D: National Forest Policy (1988) and earlier resolutions target about 33% of India's geographical area under forest cover for ecological balance—one-third norm repeated in environment syllabi. subject: History
question: The exponent of Economic Drain Theory was:
explanation: Option A matches the question because Dadabhai Naoroji systematised the 'drain of wealth' theory—arguing unrequited colonial transfers impoverished India in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule.' Ganesh Joshi, Gopal Hari Deshmukh (Lokhitwadi), and Ranade wrote on economic exploitation but Naoroji is the exponent examiners name for the drain doctrine. subject: History
question: Choose the correct pairs: List I - List II (a) Harshcharitra - (i) Kalidas (b) Maalati Madhav - (ii) Vishakhadatta (c) Malvikagnimitra - (iii) Banbhatta (d) Mudrarakshas - (iv) Bhavabhuti
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Harshacharita was written by Banabhatta (iii), Malati Madhava by Bhavabhuti (iv), Malavikagnimitram by Kalidasa (i) and Mudrarakshasa by Vishakhadatta (ii). subject: History
question: Which of the following provisions were included in the August Resolution of 1940 AD? (a) After the end of the Second World War, assistance will be provided to establish a fully responsible system of governance in India on the lines of a colony. (b) Some Indian representatives will be included in the board of the Governor General.

options.A: Option (a) is correct, option (b) is incorrect.
options.B: Option (b) is correct, option (a) is incorrect.

explanation: The verified answer here is option C. The August Offer of 1940 did promise both things — post-war help to set up a fully responsible government in India on colonial lines (a), and the inclusion of more Indians in the Governor General's council (b). Since neither statement is faulty, 'both provisions are correct' is the fit.

subject: History
question: What demands did the British Indian Association make to the British Parliament in 1853 AD on the occasion of the renewal of the Charter Act? (a) The Legislature, Executive and Judiciary should have separate jurisdictions. (b) The salaries of high-ranking officials should be reduced. (c) A new legislature should be formed and Indians should be represented in it. (d) Salt, excise and stamp duty should be abolished.
explanation: The right pick is option B. When the Charter Act came up for renewal in 1853, the British Indian Association asked for separation of the legislature, executive and judiciary, a cut in the salaries of high-ranking officials, and abolition of salt, excise and stamp duties — that is (a), (b) and (d). Forming a fresh legislature with Indian representation (c) was not part of this particular memorial, which is exactly what the other options try to slip in.

subject: History
question: Which of the following statements apply to Adilshah's Wajir Hemu? (a) Adilshah gave Hemu the title of 'Vikramjit'. (b) Hemu started his career as a Market Superintendent. (c) Hemu had not lost a single battle out of 22 battles. (d) Hemu defeated Akbar in the second battle of Panipat.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. About Hemu, statements (a), (b) and (c) hold: Adilshah gave him the title 'Vikramjit', he began as a market superintendent, and he was unbeaten in his 22 battles. Statement (d) is the odd one out, because Hemu was actually defeated at the Second Battle of Panipat (1556), not the victor over Akbar's side.

subject: History
question: Choose the correct pairs of authors: List I - List II (a) Storia-Do-Mogor - (i) Burnier (b) Travel in Mughal Empire - (ii) Niccolao Manucci (c) Early Travels in India - (iii) William Foster (d) Historical Fragment - (iv) Robert
explanation: The examiner has marked option B. Storia do Mogor is by Niccolao Manucci (ii), Travels in the Mughal Empire by Bernier (i), Early Travels in India by William Foster (iii) and the Historical Fragment by Robert (iv). Travel-account authors are a recurring MPSC favourite, so it pays to memorise them in pairs.

subject: Geography
question: Match the following: List I - List II (a) Sindhri - (i) Fertilizer Factory (b) Chittaranjan - (ii) Railway Coach Factory (c) Perambur - (iii) Locomotive Factory (d) Pimpri - (iv) Penicillin Factory
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Sindri is the fertilizer factory (i), Chittaranjan the locomotive factory (iii), Perambur the railway coach factory (ii) and Pimpri the penicillin (antibiotics) factory (iv). Location-to-industry pairs like these are pure memory marks — group them by sector while revising.

subject: History
question: Match the following Sanskrit authors of Mughal India and their works: List I - List II (a) Anantadeva - (i) Chaitanya Charitamritam (b) Gangadhara - (ii) Nirnaya Sindhu (c) Kamlakara Bhatta - (iii) Manorama (d) Krishna Das Kaviraja - (iv) Samskarakaustubha
explanation: Working through it, option B is the one. Among these Sanskrit scholars of Mughal India, Anantadeva pairs with Samskarakaustubha (iv), Gangadhara with Manorama (iii), Kamlakara Bhatta with Nirnaya Sindhu (ii) and Krishna Das Kaviraja with the Chaitanya Charitamrita (i). Krishna Das Kaviraja–Chaitanya Charitamrita is the safest anchor to start eliminating from.

subject: History
question: Who among the following was arrested in the Bhusawal Bomb Case?
explanation: The right pick is option A. Sadashiv Malkapurkar is the name linked with the arrests in the Bhusawal Bomb Case. With single-name factual questions, don't overthink the famous-sounding distractors — go with the one you have actually read in the source.

subject: History
question: __________, a Sanskrit scholar and a staunch social reformer, resigned from government service in 1864 to devote himself to the cause of social reforms.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. It was Vishnushastri Pandit, the Sanskrit scholar and staunch social reformer, who quit government service in 1864 to devote himself to social reform, particularly widow remarriage. Note the year 1864 as your quick tag for him.

subject: History
question: What are the three special practices that are included in the practice of Sufism?
explanation: The examiner has marked option D. The three special spiritual practices associated with Sufi sadhana are Mujahada, Zikr and Murakabah. The other options mix in terms like Wasl and Tawajjuh to blur the set, so lock the trio firmly.

subject: History
question: Match the following: List I - List II (a) Varahamihira - (i) Panchasiddhantika (b) Vagbhat - (ii) Ashtang Samgraha (c) Ishvara Krishna - (iii) Samkhya Karika (d) Prasatapada - (iv) Vaisheshika Sutra
explanation: The right pick is option D. Varahamihira wrote Panchasiddhantika (i), Vagbhata the Ashtanga Sangraha (ii), Ishvara Krishna the Samkhya Karika (iii) and Prashastapada the work on the Vaisheshika Sutra (iv) — a clean one-to-one order. question: Name the social reformer described in the following sentences: (a) He showed courage in practising what he preached. (b) He was a staunch supporter of women's education. explanation: The right pick is option B. subject: History
question: Match the pairs: List I - List II (a) Jiyauddin Barni - (i) Fatuh-Us-Salatin (b) Khwaja Abu Malik Isami - (ii) Kitab-Ur-Rahlah (c) Ibn Batuta - (iii) Tariq-e-Salatin Afgana (d) Ahmed Yadgar - (iv) Fatwa-e-Janhadari
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Ziauddin Barani wrote Fatwa-e-Jahandari (iv), Isami the Futuh-us-Salatin (i), Ibn Batuta the Kitab-ur-Rehla (ii) and Ahmed Yadgar the Tarikh-e-Salatin-e-Afghana (iii). Ibn Batuta–Rehla is the giveaway pair to anchor on.

explanation: The right pick is option A. Maitrakas ruled from Valabhi (i), the Chahamanas from Sakambhari (ii), the Gurjaras from Broach (iii) and the Paramaras from Dhara (iv). Capitals of early dynasties are steady scoring items — tie each dynasty to its seat of power.

subject: Geography
question: Match the regional divisions of the Himalayas (List I) with their West-East extension (List II): List I (Regional Divisions of Himalayas) - List II (West-East Extension) (a) The Punjab Himalayas - (i) Sutlej to Kali (b) The Kumaon Himalayas - (ii) Kali to Tista (c) The Nepal Himalayas - (iii) Tista to Brahmaputra (d) The Assam Himalayas - (iv) Indus to Sutlej

explanation: The right pick is option C. Rising from the surface, the layers go Troposphere (c), Tropopause (g), Stratosphere (e), Stratopause (d), Mesosphere (a), Mesopause (f) and Thermosphere (b). The trick is that each 'sphere' is capped by its 'pause' before the next sphere begins.

subject: History
question: The village agricultural lands were jointly held by the village communities and members were responsible for the payment of the land revenue. What was this system?

subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following statement/s is/are related to the Montreal Protocol? explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. subject: Science
question: Which of the following statement/s are correct? (a) There are 61 satellites to Uranus planet in the solar system. (b) The average distance of Mercury planet from the Sun is 58 million k.m. (c) The average distance from the Sun to the planet Uranus is 4495 million k.m.

subject: General Studies
question: Assertion (A): An ecosystem is a natural resource system. options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

explanation: The right pick is option A. subject: General Studies
question: Which of the following statement/s is/are not correct? (a) UN Conference on Environment and Development was held at Montreal in 1992. subject: Polity
question: With reference to the 'National Policy on the Voluntary Sector-2007', consider the following statements regarding the characteristics of Voluntary Organizations (VOs): (a) These organizations are private in nature and separate from the Government. explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. subject: Reasoning
question: Arrange the following major greenhouse gases in descending order according to the percentage of their contribution to global warming:

options.A: Carbon dioxide, Methane, Nitrous oxide, Fluorinated Gases

options.C: Methane, Carbon dioxide, Nitrous oxide, Fluorinated Gases
options.D: Methane, Nitrous oxide, Fluorinated Gases, Carbon dioxide

explanation: The verified answer here is option A. By their share in global warming, the descending order is Carbon dioxide, Methane, Nitrous oxide and then Fluorinated gases. CO2 leading and fluorinated gases trailing is the anchor that rules out the other sequences.

subject: Economy
question: Match the pairs: Poverty Eradication Programs in India - Year of launch (a) Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) - (i) 2001 (b) Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) - (ii) 1989 (c) Jawahar Rojgar Yojana - (iii) 1983 (d) Sampoorna Grameen Rojgar Yojana - (iv) 1978
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. By launch year, IRDP is 1978 (iv), RLEGP 1983 (iii), Jawahar Rojgar Yojana 1989 (ii) and Sampoorna Grameen Rojgar Yojana 2001 (i). Ordering these poverty programmes chronologically is the cleanest way to match them.

subject: Polity
question: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, which of the following statement/s is/are incorrect regarding the employment regulations for women before and after childbirth? (a) The Act mandates six weeks of leave after childbirth. (b) The Act mandates six weeks of leave before and ten weeks after childbirth. (c) The Act applies to all establishments without considering minimum number of employees. (d) The Act provides maternity and other benefits.
explanation: The right pick is option D. The incorrect statements are (b) and (c): the Maternity Benefit Act does not fix six weeks before and ten after in that form, and it does not apply to every establishment regardless of size — a minimum employee threshold applies. Statements (a) and (d) are correct, which is why (b) and (c) is the answer.

subject: Geography
question: Consider the following statements: (a) India's population density was higher than South Korea in 2017. (b) India's population density was lower than Bangladesh in 2017. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: The right pick is option B. Only statement (b) holds — in 2017 India's population density was lower than Bangladesh's, which is one of the most densely populated countries. Statement (a) fails because India's density was actually lower than, not higher than, South Korea's that year.

subject: Geography
question: Consider the following statements: Statement-I: As per projection on 1st March 2026, the total projected population of Maharashtra is about 12.93 crore. Statement-II: During the same period, the urban population of Maharashtra is higher than its rural population. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?

options.A: Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect.
options.B: Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct.
options.C: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
options.D: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.

explanation: The verified answer here is option A. Statement-I is right — Maharashtra's projected population on 1 March 2026 is about 12.93 crore — but Statement-II is wrong, since the urban population is not projected to exceed the rural population for that period. So Statement-I correct, Statement-II incorrect.

subject: Economy
question: Social security measures are typically divided into two main categories. Which of the following best represents these categories? (a) Social insurance (b) Social welfare (c) Social assistance (d) Social inclusion
explanation: Working through it, option C is the one. Social security is usually split into two broad heads — social insurance (a) and social assistance (c). Social welfare and social inclusion are wider ideas, not the two core categories, so (a) and (c) is the tidy pair.

subject: Economy
question: The periods of the First and Fourth Five Year Plans are __________ and __________ respectively.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option B. The First Five Year Plan ran 1951-56 and the Fourth Five Year Plan ran 1969-74. The gap before the Fourth Plan (the 'plan holiday' of 1966-69) is the detail that fixes 1969 as its start.

subject: Economy
question: Consider the following statements regarding the Public Distribution System (PDS) in Maharashtra: (a) By December 2025, there were 270.48 lakh ration card holders in the state. (b) As of 31 October 2025, 51,636 Fair price shops were functioning in the state. (c) By October 2025, about 1.55 crore families received food grains through Aadhaar-based biometric authentication. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The verified answer here is option B. Statements (b) and (c) are correct — about 51,636 fair price shops functioning as of 31 October 2025, and roughly 1.55 crore families served via Aadhaar-based biometric authentication by October 2025. Statement (a)'s ration-card-holder figure does not match, so only (b) and (c) stand.

subject: Economy
question: As pointed out by the Tendulkar Committee, the concept of poverty is associated with socially perceived deprivation with respect to basic human needs like __________. (a) the need to be adequately nourished (b) the need to be reasonably sheltered (c) the need to be decently clothed (d) the need to escape avoidable diseases (e) the need to be minimally educated Which of the above point/s is/are correct?
explanation: The verified answer here is option D. The Tendulkar Committee framed poverty around socially perceived deprivation across all these needs — adequate nourishment, reasonable shelter, decent clothing, escape from avoidable disease and minimal education. Since every point belongs to the list, 'all of the above' is the fit.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following are disadvantages of subdivision and fragmentation of land holding? (a) Wastage of Land (b) Disguised Unemployment (c) Easy to Land Management (d) Low Productivity
explanation: The right pick is option B. Fragmentation of holdings brings wastage of land (a), disguised unemployment (b) and low productivity (d). Statement (c) — 'easy land management' — is actually a benefit, not a drawback, so it drops out and (a), (b) and (d) remain.

subject: Economy
question: On the basis of Tendulkar Committee estimation, __________% of the rural population and __________% of the urban population was below the poverty line in 2004-05.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option A. On the Tendulkar Committee's 2004-05 estimate, 41.8% of the rural and 25.7% of the urban population were below the poverty line. Keep the rural figure higher than the urban one as a sanity check against the swapped distractors.

subject: Economy
question: Which of the following statement/s is/are correct regarding National Food Security Act - 2013? (a) Women empowerment is a feature of the National Food Security Act - 2013. (b) State Food Commission is the monitoring, reviewing and implementing authority of this Act - 2013.
explanation: The right pick is option A. Statement (a) is correct — women empowerment is a built-in feature of the National Food Security Act, 2013, which treats the eldest woman as the head of the household for the ration card. Statement (b)'s description of the State Food Commission's role does not match the Act's wording, so only (a) stands.

subject: Economy
question: Consider the following statements: (a) In the overall Capital Stock, David Pearce and Jeremy Warford include man-made physical capital, human capital and environmental capital. (b) According to David Pearce and Jeremy Warford, sustainable development implies that man-made physical capital, human capital and environmental capital decrease in the growth process. Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
explanation: Working through it, option A is the one. Statement (a) is correct — Pearce and Warford count man-made physical, human and environmental capital within the overall capital stock. Statement (b) reverses their idea: sustainable development does not require these to decrease in the growth process, so only (a) is right.

subject: Science
question: The net electric charge that passes through the surface per unit time is called __________.
explanation: The right pick is option A. Net electric charge crossing a surface per unit time is, by definition, the electric current. The other terms describe voltage or motion, not the rate of charge flow, so 'electric current' is the clean answer.

subject: Economy
question: Consider the following statements in the context of the aims of the National Population Policy, 2000: (a) Promote delayed marriage for girls, not earlier than age 18 and preferably after 21 years of age. (b) The long-term objective is to achieve a stable population by 2030. Which of the statement/s given above is/are incorrect?
explanation: The examiner has marked option C. Both statements are wrong here — the age framing in (a) does not match the National Population Policy 2000's actual aim, and the long-term stable-population target in the policy is set for 2045, not 2030 as in (b). So both (a) and (b) are incorrect.

subject: Science
question: Match the quantities in Column I with their dimensions in Column II: Column I - Column II (a) Permeability (μ₀) - (i) ML²T⁻¹ (b) Coefficient of Viscosity (η) - (ii) MLT⁻²I⁻² (c) Planck's Constant (h) - (iii) ML⁻¹T⁻¹ (Where M is mass, L is length, T is time and I is the current)
explanation: The verified answer here is option C. Permeability μ₀ carries the dimensions MLT⁻²I⁻² (ii), the coefficient of viscosity η is ML⁻¹T⁻¹ (iii) and Planck's constant h is ML²T⁻¹ (i). Deriving each dimension from a defining formula is safer than memorising the whole grid.

subject: Science
question: If the refractive index of the medium is more than the refractive index of a double concave or double convex lens, then the focal length of the lens becomes __________.
explanation: Straight to the answer — option D. If the surrounding medium has a higher refractive index than the lens, the lens's behaviour reverses and its focal length turns negative. This is why a convex lens can act divergent inside a denser medium — a favourite conceptual twist.

subject: Science
question: According to the Second Law of thermodynamics, how much will be the efficiency of a heat engine?
explanation: The right pick is option D. By the Second Law of thermodynamics, no heat engine can be perfectly efficient — some heat is always rejected — so its efficiency is always less than one. 'One' would mean a perfect engine, which the law forbids.
